description: Hi! I am Saif, an independent writer and space enthusiast participating solo in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. I love creative writing and storytelling. Through my project, I want to share inspiring and educational stories about NASA's space exploration and the equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.
summary: Silent Sacrifice: NASA's Mission to Find Water on the Moon is an illustrated storytelling project for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Told from the first-person perspective of NASA’s Atlas V Centaur upper stage, the story chronicles the June 18, 2009 launch of LRO and LCROSS, their 4.5-day journey to the Moon, and their daring October 9, 2009 impact into the -240°C shadows of Cabeus crater. By kicking up a plume of lunar dust, LCROSS confirmed 155 kilograms of water vapor and ice before crashing onto the lunar surface. Though their hardware rests silently on the Moon today, their sacrifice mapped the water resources that will guide future NASA Artemis astronauts on the next frontier.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works Silent Sacrifice: NASA's Mission to Find Water on the Moon is a 7-slide illustrated comic storytelling deck created for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Told from the first-person perspective of NASA’s Atlas V Centaur upper stage, the story guides readers through the June 18, 2009 launch of LRO and LCROSS, their 4.5-day (384,400 km) voyage to lunar orbit, and their daring October 9, 2009 impact at 9,000 km/h into the -240°C shadows of Cabeus crater—which confirmed 155 kilograms of lunar water vapor and ice.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact • Accessible Space Education: Transforms complex orbital mechanics and NASA telemetry data into an emotional, easy-to-read visual story for students and young learners. • Honoring Silent Pioneers: Raises global awareness about the discarded space hardware resting on the Moon that mapped water resources for NASA’s Artemis program and the 2026 theme, "The Next Frontier."

3. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used • Coding Languages: None (this is a non-coding storytelling and visual narrative project). • Official Data Sources: Verified mission archives from NASA Science (LRO, LCROSS, and Artemis). • Software & Hardware: Produced on a mobile device using Canva / Google Slides for layout and PDF compilation. Generative AI tools were used responsibly to create custom comic illustrations (Slides 2–6) and assist with English translation from the author's original script.

4. How the Project Is Creative Instead of presenting dry historical dates, the project personifies the Atlas V Centaur rocket as a brave narrator sharing its sacrifice alongside its twin explorers, LRO and LCROSS. Combining custom comic-book artwork with authentic NASA mission milestones creates an engaging storybook format that connects emotionally with readers.

5. Factors Considered by the Team • Scientific Precision: Every number, timeline, and measurement (-240°C crater temperature, 113-day flight, 155 kg water ice) was strictly verified against NASA archives. • Realistic Future Outlook: Clearly distinguished between past discoveries and future goals, noting that humans have not yet harvested this water while highlighting its value for upcoming Artemis astronauts. • Clarity & Transparency: Designed with high-contrast text boxes for easy reading alongside full disclosure of NASA sources and AI visual assistance.
